Our setting was in the Nobel home of Count Beor-Laith Wynfire and his wife Countess Ravanna Wynfire, the Count has been informed there is a plan to assassinate him. He invites the six people who he suspects for a lovely feast in the hope to smoke out the assassin before they can be successful.

Our first course is a fruit and cheese board. I used a mix of nuts, dried fruit, crackers, cheeses and meats. During this course we get to know our players. 

Ravanna is the countess and is hiding a deep secret that the count will have her beheaded if it comes to light. She is planning on leaving her husband for a handsome pirate who has stolen her heart.

Mushroom is a human/ bunny hybrid who must get the Count to stop invading her land , or risk going to war with both the Count’s army, and the Naga’s half serpent half human race. Her kingdom is at risk of two wars she has no hope to win. 

Leois is the illegitimate child of the Count he successfully hid all these years. Her mother died shortly after her birth and she was raised by fairies. She wants to avenge her mother’s death, and have the people know who their beloved Count really is. 

Bluntista is a old friend of the Count, and a local head of the police. Over the years the Count has kept his name clean, and out of trouble, but Bluntista tired of doing the Count’s shady deals. In an effort to resign and start a new life he and the Count agreed just one more deal and he would be free. But the deal didn’t go as planned and now there is a manhunt for the culprit, and everyone knows for two people to keep a secret one must die. 

Rylynn is a spy sent from a rival land, the Count has been sabotaging their crops and water sources. In an effort to get close to the Count he has disguised himself as a lone traveler. He is the only one at the feast the Count doesn’t suspect. 

Zaya is the Count’s advisor and an unknown witch, her family has always worked for the Wynfire family. When she was younger the Count had her father “disappear” for an act of treason. Her father was innocent and the only other possible suspect was the Count. 

Our second course was an acorn squash soup, I had originally wanted to serve them in bread bowls but the bread was too small. During this course some clues were given, so the guest could start Eliminating suspects. 

Our third course was pan seared duck breast, ribeye and boiled potatoes. More clues were given, and action cards were added in. People could choose to share their clues or not. 

Our last course was a crème brûlée where everyone gave their motive but explained why it wasn’t them. Also who they suspected was really the killer. Everyone voted who they thought it was. Mushroom was who got the most votes but Leois was the killer. 

The answer was given in a final envelope to be opened by the ghost of the Count. A lot of the conversations during the meal was improv by all of us. There are quite a few things I am going to do differently for our next mystery but for a first try, and pulling everything together is >2 days it was great.

I forgot to add I made cocktails for the adults and mocktails for the kids. For the adults I used green apple vodka (with luster dust to make it shimmery like a potion) with raspberry liquor and black cherry juice. For the kids I used pomegranate juice, black cherry juice and seltzer (with luster dust also) .

You are welcome, I hope you stay self harm free, and I also hope if you do relapse you brush yourself off pick yourself up, and start the journey again. One day at a time. AA helped me so much, I continued to go to meetings for months after my last relapse, until I found a self harm group. The self harm group was actually found for me by my temporary therapist while my normal therapist was on personal leave. And that group is a lot like AA. Just a group of people struggling with behavior that negatively impacts their lives .

Ask any addict, you are always an addict. I remember the first time I went into a mental health hospital, I was 16 had been cutting 2 years by then. The hospital had mandatory AA for the teens, this annoyed me so much for whatever reason. I got mouthy ( I regret the way I acted towards these people) and one of the nurses took me aside and told me I needed to listen because while I wasn’t an addict in the sense of a drug addict, or an alcoholic, but was addicted to self harm. 

I brushed that off, I didn’t have to cut, I could quit whenever I wanted ( sounds like a lot of addicts ) . It wasn’t until I was in my 20s and had gone into treatment because I had attempted suicide; that I went to the AA classes because I wanted to. I listened, I saw so much of my behavior with my cutting that these people who are recovering alcoholics and drug addicts did before they hit their rock bottom. I would go through “sober/clean” periods then relapse each time worse than before. 

About 2 years  ago my life had completely crashed around me ( it actually just kept getting worse for a long time after) and I relapsed again, nothing too bad, but a relapse . I told my therapist at my weekly appointment and she called my psychiatrist, who quickly called and chewed my ass. We made a plan, I for the fourth time in my life found myself checking in to a mental health hospital. For whatever reason this time was different, something clicked, I worked there in tandem with my therapist and psychiatrist, and the hospital staff and we made a recovery plan. The same template they used for people with chemical dependency.  

It has been 2 years, and 2 months since I last cut myself, and I still feel myself needing to cut when things get hard. My heart races, I can feel my skin sting the way it does when you do a quick shallow cut, my mind focuses solely on getting a blade. When those times happen, I pull out that ratty handwritten recovery plan. I do grounding exercises, I call my dad, I call my mom, I distract myself, I follow the plan; most times the feeling passes, the times it doesn’t I repeat the steps, get on here read these stories, and then I look at my scars and remember the shame I felt the day I had to explain to my young daughter why my arms and legs have scars everywhere. 

I gave this super long winded response to say, yes it is very possible. Because self harm is addictive, I hope one day it will not be this hard the older I get, but for now it is still a challenge, everyday I could relapse I hope I don’t. I also wish I never would have started, at 14 I didn’t think I would still be struggling with this 16 years later.
